problem: Portal V2 had strong functional coverage but visual scale, media sizing, chart containment and interaction consistency were still governed by multiple page-specific styles, allowing oversized components and inconsistent responsive behavior.
rootCause: Portal UX quality had been distributed across page-specific styles and separate candidate experience ideas. Consolidating those controls into the existing experience authority prevents parallel UI stacks and makes responsive/runtime regressions machine-detectable.
preventionRule: Portal V2 has one shared experience authority. Every current and dynamic view inherits responsive sizing, 44px critical touch targets, visible focus, reduced-motion support, overflow measurement, runtime signaling and the 24-case visual assurance matrix while Portal State remains the backend authority.
